review_status: draft v1 - deep reef grouper profile

profile.behavior: Favors deep, high-relief coral ledges and rocky drop-offs along the outer continental shelf.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, favorable for scamp grouper.
factors.value_notes: A southeastern U.S. spawning survey recorded spawning scamp at bottom temperatures of 16–27 °C (mean 21.0 °C); a SEDAR assessment describes spawning off the Carolinas at 22–25 °C. These are seasonal bottom-water/spawning observations, not a general adult SST preference curve; they partially overlap but do not validate 18–27 °C / 20–24 °C as a year-round surface-temperature optimum.

SEDAR and SAFMC describe scamp using low-profile live-bottom areas, Oculina coral, ledges, and high-relief rocky bottoms; wrecks and rock outcrops are also used. This supports the broad reef/ledge/wreck association but does not validate the exact category ranking or score values.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in deep shelf edge habitat.
factors.value_notes: SAFMC reports preferred low-profile live-bottom habitat at 75–300 ft (about 23–91 m); FishBase reports 30–100 m and NOAA/SEDAR sources describe broad shelf habitat. This overlaps the configured 25–100 m / 40–80 m band, but does not validate the exact ideal interval or all regional/life-stage differences. Depth is an active gate.

text.day: It is full daylight, when fish feed actively.
text.dawn: It is dawn, a low-light time when fish feed actively.
text.dusk: It is dusk, a low-light time when fish feed actively.

timing.note: Patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies.
